the indiscriminate use of antibiotics is not only wasteful but may be harmful to patients.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the results of the drug sensitivity tests performed in our laboratory have been of value in the management of patients with bacterial infections, and have contributed to the prevention of the untoward effects of chemotherapy.
it is possible to achieve a high degree of cure and a low incidence of toxicity in a general practice by the use of chemotherapy guided by the results of drug sensitivity tests.

the use of chemotherapy in general practice should be restricted to patients with a positive culture and a drug sensitivity test, or to those with a history of a positive culture or of hypersensitivity to a drug, or to those whose condition is so serious that a trial of a single drug is justified.
The main takeaway from our work is that

we have shown that we can use the same drugs that are used to treat cancer in the clinic, in the context of a mouse model, and we can do so without the use of chemotherapy drugs, which is the current standard.
the current approach for drug sensitivity testing in cancer patients is not optimal.
the drug sensitivity tests can be done at home, in a very short time, and with very simple and easily available materials.
